learningObjective: Explain how a PagedAttention kernel differs from a FlashAttention kernel and what block-table indirection costs at execution time.

canonicalClaims.claim: PagedAttention adds a block-table lookup to a FlashAttention-style kernel: per KV block, look up its physical HBM address in the per-sequence block table, then stream that block into SMEM and run standard online-softmax attention math. Overhead is per-block, not per-element.
conditions: Block table small enough to fit alongside KV blocks in HBM.
nonImplications: Does not imply a gather-to-contiguous step.

misconceptions.claim: PagedAttention gathers scattered blocks into a contiguous buffer before attention math.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Blocks are loaded directly into SMEM; no gather-to-contiguous step.

misconceptions.claim: PagedAttention is an approximate sparse attention.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It is exact; paging refers to memory layout only.

misconceptions.claim: PagedAttention stores KV in host memory.
misconceptions.whyWrong: KV lives in HBM; the page table maps virtual position to HBM block.

implementationFacts: vLLM ships two PagedAttention kernel variants (v1, v2) with different tiling strategies.
FlashAttention with paged KV cache is also supported (FlashAttention-2 has a paged mode).
performanceScenarios: Measured PagedAttention latency is within a few percent of contiguous FlashAttention in production.
